storage: Fallback cache only. Open/closed classifications in the fallback are not certified current; NHTSA full-source refresh replaces them on deployment.

investigations.subject: Child pedestrian struck near elementary school
investigations.summary: NHTSA opened a preliminary evaluation after a driverless Waymo vehicle struck a child who ran from behind a double-parked SUV near a Santa Monica elementary school during drop-off on January 23, 2026; the child had minor injuries. NHTSA will examine whether the system showed appropriate caution, its school-zone behavior and speed-limit adherence, and its response after impact.

investigations.subject: Passing stopped school buses
investigations.summary: NHTSA opened a preliminary evaluation after a media report that a driverless Waymo vehicle drove around a stopped school bus in Atlanta on September 22, 2025, passing the bus's extended stop arm and crossing control arm near disembarking students. NHTSA is examining how Waymo's system is designed to obey school-bus laws and whether similar incidents occurred across about 2,000 vehicles.

investigations.subject: Tesla Cybercab federal safety certification audit
investigations.summary: NHTSA opened an audit query into Tesla's certification of the Cybercab, which lacks conventional steering, braking, and accelerator controls. Investigators are examining the technical basis for Tesla's claim that the vehicle complies with federal motor vehicle safety standards, including whether Tesla considered certain standards inapplicable.

investigations.subject: Traffic-safety violations with FSD engaged
investigations.product: Tesla vehicles equipped with FSD (Supervised) or FSD (Beta)
investigations.summary: NHTSA opened a preliminary evaluation covering about 2.9 million Tesla vehicles with Full Self-Driving (Supervised or Beta) after complaints, crash reports and media reports alleging red-light running and entry into opposing lanes, including crashes with injuries. NHTSA will assess whether drivers received enough warning and time to supervise and intervene.

investigations.subject: FSD collisions in reduced roadway visibility
investigations.summary: NHTSA upgraded its probe of Tesla Full Self-Driving in poor visibility to an engineering analysis covering about 3.2 million vehicles, citing nine crashes, one fatal, in glare and airborne obscurants. It will assess whether the system's degradation-detection feature recognizes reduced camera visibility and alerts drivers in time, including Tesla's later software update.

investigations.subject: Unexpected ADS behavior
investigations.summary: NHTSA opened a preliminary evaluation of Waymo's fifth-generation driving system after 22 incidents, 17 of them crashes without injuries, in which vehicles struck gates, chains or parked cars, or appeared to disobey traffic control devices. It will evaluate how the system detects and responds to traffic controls and avoids stationary objects, across about 444 vehicles.

investigations.subject: Unexpected ADS braking
investigations.summary: NHTSA opened a preliminary evaluation after two incidents in which Zoox-operated Toyota Highlanders braked suddenly and were rear-ended by following motorcyclists, causing minor injuries. NHTSA is evaluating the Zoox driving system's performance in those collisions, around crosswalk pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and in similar rear-end scenarios, covering about 500 vehicles.

investigations.subject: Purpose-built vehicle certification
investigations.summary: NHTSA's audit query examined whether Zoox properly self-certified its purpose-built, control-free vehicle as compliant with federal safety standards; a December 2024 inspection report found multiple apparent noncompliances. It closed August 4, 2025 after NHTSA granted Zoox a conditional demonstration exemption that requires it to remove claims of full compliance.

investigations.subject: ADS behavior around pedestrians
investigations.summary: NHTSA's preliminary evaluation examined whether Cruise's driverless vehicles took appropriate caution around pedestrians after two pedestrian crashes and public reports of vehicles encroaching on crosswalks. It closed January 14, 2025 after Cruise's recall 23E-086 of 950 vehicles, which fixed software that could pull over after striking a pedestrian, and after Cruise ceased operations.

investigations.subject: Hard braking and immobilizations
investigations.summary: NHTSA's preliminary evaluation reviewed 7,632 hard-braking events and vehicle immobilizations by Cruise's driverless vehicles, which contributed to 10 reported crashes, four injuring vulnerable road users; no immobilization caused a crash or injury. It closed August 20, 2024 after Cruise's recall 24E-067 and software updates to reduce unexpected braking.

investigations.subject: Autopilot driver engagement and misuse
investigations.summary: NHTSA's engineering analysis of about 2.0 million Tesla vehicles found that Autopilot's weak driver-engagement controls, paired with high control authority, led to foreseeable misuse and avoidable crashes, including at least 13 fatal ones. It closed April 25, 2024 after Tesla's recall 23V-838; NHTSA then opened recall query RQ24009 to assess whether the remedy is effective.
